latest_apis.rationale: Every individual API used is current and stable in 16.4.3, and the version itself is exactly current. But the data-loading model is the one Vercel now brands 'Previous Model' and will replace by default in 17, so the app sits one major release behind the framework's direction.

Not a 5 because the caching layer re-implements what the framework's use cache/cacheLife now provide, and sprite URLs are plain string concatenation (PokemonCard.tsx:11-13).

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts — all HTTP access, 404 mapping and list walking behind one module; a PokeAPI change touches one file
app/src/lib/format.ts — pure, shared server/client helpers instead of duplicated inline logic
app/src/lib/api.ts:46 — api<T = any> default: the API response shape is untyped at the boundary
app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:58-111 — getMoves(pokemon: any) and any-typed map/sort callbacks throughout the page
app/src/components/PokemonCard.tsx:16 and app/src/components/TypeBadge.tsx:12 — prefetch={false} on every link, silently opting out of framework navigation optimizations with no comment
churn_resistance.rationale: Centralized data access and pure helpers localize most change, and nothing depends on framework internals. But the untyped any boundary means upstream API changes fail at runtime rather than compile time, and the bespoke TTL cache is the one piece a Next 17 upgrade rewrites.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled in-memory Map cache (TTL, promise dedup, LRU-ish prune) on top of fetch cache:'no-store' — this is the 'Previous Model' of data fetching, superseded by cacheComponents + 'use cache'/cacheLife which Next 16.4 now recommends and 17 makes the default.
findings.suggestion: Adopt cacheComponents: true + partialPrefetching: true in next.config.ts, mark api()/getTypeRecords() etc. with 'use cache' and a short cacheLife profile, and delete the custom cache. Keeps request-time freshness while removing the hand-rolled layer that a Next 17 upgrade would force anyway.

findings.issue: Pervasive any typing at the API boundary (getMoves(pokemon: any), any-typed sort/map callbacks) leaves the raw PokeAPI shape unchecked; upstream changes surface as runtime bugs.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API payloads consumed (Species, Pokemon, MoveRecord, VersionGroup) in lib/api.ts and let api<T> default to them or require the type argument.

findings.issue: URL state is written via window.history.replaceState with manual pathname+search+hash reassembly rather than the router's URL helpers; works because App Router syncs with the history API, but the hash-assembly logic is brittle hand-rolling.
findings.suggestion: Use `url.href` (or router.replace with scroll:false) and keep only one place per page that owns query-string serialization.

findings.issue: prefetch={false} on nearly every Link in the app disables the framework's optimized prefetching (incremental/partial prefetching in 16.x) with no recorded reason.
findings.suggestion: Either enable prefetch for card/type links (they are the app's main navigation) or leave a comment explaining the deliberate opt-out so a future maintainer re-evaluates it.

findings.issue: new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString()) round-trips an object that already exposes .get(); redundant conversion.
findings.suggestion: Read filters directly from the ReadonlyURLSearchParams passed to readFilters.

findings.issue: Pagination uses raw <a> plus manual pushState, preventDefault and window.scrollTo instead of next/link — hand-rolled router integration that a framework update or a11y review could invalidate.
findings.suggestion: Use <Link> with scroll handling (scroll={true}) or document that plain anchors are chosen to avoid RSC round-trips for purely client-side filtering.

summary: A clean, minimal App Router app pinned to the exact current stable Next.js and using current stable APIs (connection(), async params, metadata/viewport split), with all data access funneled through one typed-enough module and only three runtime dependencies. The central forward-looking weakness is that its entire data layer — fetch with no-store plus a hand-rolled TTL cache, fully dynamic pages, no use of cacheComponents/'use cache' or streaming shells — is the model the framework now labels 'Previous Model' and flips defaults on in Next 17. Combined with an untyped any boundary against the upstream API, an upgrade will be localized but real; acceptable today, slightly behind the curve tomorrow.

apis.api: fetch cache:'no-store' + custom in-memory cache (previous data model)
apis.replacement: cacheComponents: true with 'use cache' + cacheLife, recommended for all apps as of Next 16.4 (nextjs.org/blog/next-16-4), default in Next 17
